I need to send a quarterly update to our investors. I'm the founder of a scheduling app for physical therapy clinics. We have 6 people.

Numbers for the quarter:
- Monthly recurring revenue is $41,000, the same as three months ago.
- We added 9 clinics and lost 4. One of the 4 was our largest customer, a 12-clinic chain that paid $5,500 a month. They moved to the scheduler built into their electronic records system.
- We have $480,000 in the bank and lose about $44,000 a month.
- Clinics that use our automatic text reminders have a no-show rate of 7%, against 13% before they started.
- I didn't send updates for the last two quarters.
- Next month we start selling the reminder feature on its own for $150 a month.

Under 500 words. It goes to 11 investors.

Runway works out to about 11 months ($480K ÷ $44K). The update says that plainly, because investors will do the math themselves.

Subject: [Company] Q3 update, and an apology for the silence

Hi all,

First, an apology. I didn't send updates for the last two quarters. That's on me, and you'll hear from me every quarter from now on.

The short version: revenue was flat this quarter because we lost our largest customer. We have about 11 months of runway. Our text reminder feature is clearly working, and next month we start selling it on its own.

**The numbers**
- MRR: $41,000 (flat vs. three months ago)
- New clinics: 9
- Customers lost: 4, including our largest
- Cash: $480,000
- Net burn: ~$44,000/month
- Runway: ~11 months
- Team: 6

**What happened**
Our largest customer, a 12-clinic chain paying $5,500/month, moved to the scheduler built into their electronic records system. New clinics made up for that loss and the other three, so MRR held steady. But we didn't grow.

This is the risk I take most seriously. Records vendors are bundling scheduling, and multi-site chains are the most likely to consolidate onto one system. Competing as a standalone scheduler against a free built-in option is a hard position, and this quarter showed it.

**What's working**
Clinics using our automatic text reminders have a 7% no-show rate, down from 13% before they started. That removes nearly half of their missed appointments. A no-show is a slot the clinic usually can't refill, so owners can put a dollar figure on this.

**What's next**
Next month we start selling reminders as a standalone product at $150/month. This lets us sell to clinics that already have a scheduler, including the ones built into their records system, instead of competing with it. The customer we just lost is exactly the kind of clinic this is built for.

Next quarter I'll report on standalone reminder signups, MRR growth, and churn.

**Runway**
At current burn we have about 11 months. [Your plan: e.g., raising in Q_, reducing burn to $__K, or reaching $__K MRR by __.] I'll share progress against this in every update.

**How you can help**
- Introductions to physical therapy clinic owners or operators, especially those using a records system with built-in scheduling. They're the first customers for standalone reminders.
- If you've seen a company handle a larger platform bundling its core product, I'd value 20 minutes of your time.

Thank you for your patience and your support.

[Your name]
</final_document>

A few things to check before sending:

- **Runway plan:** I left a placeholder because investors will see 11 months and want to know your plan. Even one sentence helps, such as "raising in Q2" or "cutting burn to reach break-even." Leaving it blank will raise more questions than a modest plan would.
- **The quarterly promise:** keep it only if you'll stick to it. Missing another update after this apology would hurt more than the first two did.
- **Clinic counts:** I wrote "9 new clinics" and "4 customers lost" because it's unclear whether the chain counts as 1 clinic or 12. Adjust the wording if you track this differently.
- **The asks** are my suggestions. Swap them for whatever you actually need.
